heroHeadline: South Korea Monitors North Korean Border Incursions, Maintains Military Readiness
heroSubtitle: South Korea's Defense Intelligence Agency said August 23, 2026 — its first public comment on the reports since October 2024 — that North Korea continues preparing for an additional troop deployment to Russia but detected no signs one is imminent, assessing more than 16,000 DPRK troops sent cumulatively and over 15 million rounds of 152mm-equivalent artillery shells supplied. Two days later, Kim Jong-un presided over the fourth enlarged meeting of the Workers' Party political bureau in Pyongyang to review the new five-year economic plan, calling for 'extraordinary responsibility and high prudence' after citing 'a series of deviations' from immature economic guidance — notably making no mention of President Trump's ongoing overtures for a possible summit, which followed North Korea's 12th weapons test of the year on August 20 and the early conclusion of the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise on August 21.
footerNote: Data sourced from US/ROK official reports, KCNA, UN panels, IAEA, and institutional analyses. North Korea does not publish national statistics — economic figures are estimates with wide uncertainty ranges.
